title: Efficient and Effective Anchored Densest Subgraph Search: A Convex-programming based Approach

problem.claim: The task is to identify local dense communities connected to predetermined seed nodes.

gap.claim: The state-of-the-art anchored densest subgraph model often struggles to efficiently uncover truly dense communities.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes an NR-subgraph density metric for identifying communities linked to seed nodes while maintaining high overall graph density.
The paper reformulates anchored densest subgraph search as a linear programming problem and derives a dual convex-programming formulation.
The paper proposes FDP for near-optimal solutions and FDPE for exact convergence.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the NR-subgraph density metric as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on 12 real-world networks.
The authors report that their algorithms outperform state-of-the-art methods by 3.6–14.1 times in running time and produce subgraphs with superior internal quality.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dense community search around predetermined seed nodes is important across applications.
The existing anchored densest subgraph model uses R-subgraph density but has efficiency and density limitations.
The paper introduces NR-subgraph density and formulates the resulting search problem through linear programming and its dual.
Two algorithms are proposed: FDP for near-optimal solutions and FDPE for exact convergence.
Experiments on 12 real-world networks report faster runtimes and higher internal subgraph quality than state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The proposed density metric combines seed-node connection with overall graph density.

interpretation.claim: A task-specific objective can address a mismatch between existing optimization criteria and the desired community structure.

application.claim: When searching for communities anchored to known seeds, evaluate objectives that balance anchor relevance and internal cohesion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this metric generalizes beyond the evaluated networks or applications.

source_observation.claim: The method provides both a near-optimal iterative algorithm and an exact convergent algorithm.

interpretation.claim: Providing accuracy–efficiency alternatives can support different operational constraints.

application.claim: Use a fast approximate solver when speed is prioritized and an exact solver when full convergence is required.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the runtime or scalability trade-off between FDP and FDPE.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal NR-subgraph density equation.
The abstract does not report dataset identities, network sizes, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide absolute runtimes, quality metrics, or variance estimates.
The abstract does not describe the convex-programming algorithm details or convergence guarantees beyond the stated descriptions.
